rationale: Two subtests, and only the second can be failing: tcase 1 (open of a missing file without O_CREAT -> ENOENT) is core path resolution that many already-green tests exercise, so the defect is tcase 2 -- unprivileged open(O_RDONLY|O_NOATIME) must return EPERM. Asterinas accepts O_NOATIME as a status flag (fs/file/file_attr/status_flags.rs:22, and it is in SETFL_MASK at :35 and SettableStatusFlags::minimal at :51) but performs no owner-or-capable check on it anywhere: grep NOATIME across kernel/src returns only the mount-flag plumbing and the bitflag definitions, never a credential test. Linux does this once, in do_dentry_open (fs/open.c): O_NOATIME requires inode_owner_or_capable(), else -EPERM. So this is one missing check at one call site, and the in-tree precedent for writing it is already there -- fs/vfs/path/mod.rs:306-312 and fs/vfs/path/dentry.rs:487 both do the euid-vs-inode-uid-else-CapSet::FOWNER test. That is narrow syscall semantics rather than an absent subsystem. Ground no earlier round covered: rounds 1-3 of this invocation took statfs03 (VFS check_permission), epoll_ctl05 (epoll interest graph) and semctl02 (SysV IPC permission stub), and across all 33 prior runs nothing has touched O_NOATIME or the open-time credential check. open04 is the same syscall but a different layer (FileTable RLIMIT_NOFILE) and is on an unmerged branch. Runners-up rejected on evidence: mprotect01 is recorded tbroke/broken in Asterinas by three independent runs (run-STzXZ3, run-5G5q5b, run-dCeGov) so it aborts in setup, and its EACCES subtest needs VM_MAYWRITE-style tracking of the mapped file's open mode, i.e. two defects not one; splice01/splice02/tee01 have no syscall handler at all in kernel/src/syscall (only sendfile.rs), a missing feature; fcntl12 is the same RLIMIT_NOFILE defect as open04; fcntl17/23/27 are file leases and record locks; utimes01/utime06 need needs_rofs; creat08/creat09/open10 are the S_ISGID inheritance defect already diagnosed by mkdir02; the semctl/semop cluster is round 3's IPC stub; epoll_ctl04 and the epoll_wait cluster are round 2's ground; the accept/connect/send/recv/setsockopt cluster is blocked on the INADDR_ANY missing feature per run-OgXQbF.
notes: No Asterinas probe boot was needed: select.cache already holds probe fail records for open02 on exactly this run's base_commit e8f2b9ca6, from two independent runs (run-STzXZ3 and run-UceFMi), which cache.md rates usable as-is at the same commit. Host baseline re-measured for this run out of /nix/store/hik6kb512ia3p14lc2vwzb292d4k306a-ltp-20260529/testcases/bin: 2 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken / 0 skipped, with 'open02.c:47: TPASS: open() unprivileged O_RDONLY | O_NOATIME : EPERM (1)' -- so the EPERM is real Linux behaviour on the pinned version, not a test artifact. Which subtest fails in Asterinas is cached only at whole-test granularity; confirming it is tcase 2 is diagnose's job. Verify configuration is the default because the entry comes from all.txt, hence run_vars is empty -- no CONFORMANCE_TEST_WORKDIR and no extra blocklist. Test source: /nix/store/6is5pwis1dp779rjcf6n5kgyp6xlrmln-source/testcases/kernel/syscalls/open/open02.c (99 lines incl. the 20260529 tree's setup that touches the file as root at mode 0644, then SAFE_SETEUID to nobody, so the target file is owned by another uid and the caller keeps read permission through the other-r bit). Adjacent line all.txt:999 '# open04' stays commented and is out of scope.
